extracted.intended_audience: NSF-funded institutions, research administrators, principal investigators, mentors, trainees (undergraduate/graduate students, postdocs), and other senior personnel supported by NSF
extracted.subtask_description: NSF guidance describing institutional responsibilities, required training and oversight, and related policies for the responsible and ethical conduct of research (RECR) for personnel supported by NSF. Includes links to related regulatory areas and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible and Ethical Conduct of Research (RECR) — rigor and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: RECR involves a responsibility to generate and disseminate knowledge with rigor and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching expectation for NSF-supported research: work must be conducted and communicated with scientific rigor and integrity to maintain excellence and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct peer review with the highest ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct peer review with the highest ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers must follow ethical norms (e.g., confidentiality, impartiality, conflict disclosure) when evaluating proposals and manuscripts; NSF provides further merit review and panelist COI guidance linked on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect proprietary information and intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently protect proprietary information and intellectual property from inappropriate disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and institutions must safeguard confidential/proprietary data and IP, controlling disclosures consistent with sponsor requirements and institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat students and colleagues fairly and with respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat students and colleagues fairly and with respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional conduct expectations include fair treatment, respect, and fostering inclusive, harassment-free working and learning environments; related OCR and harassment resources are referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education in RECR is essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Education in RECR is considered essential in the preparation of future scientists and engineers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF emphasizes that training in ethical and responsible research practices is a core part of preparing trainees and early-career researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional RECR training and oversight plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF requires institutions to have a plan to provide appropriate training and oversight in the responsible and ethical conduct of research for undergraduate students, graduate students, postdoctoral scholars, faculty, and other senior personnel who will be supported by NSF to conduct research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The training must include mentor training and mentorship. For more information institutions should refer to the Proposal and Award Policies and Procedures Guide (PAPPG), Chapter IX.B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference: Proposal and Award Policies and Procedures Guide (PAPPG) Chapter IX.B
rubrics_metrics.description: For more information about RECR training and the oversight responsibilities of institutions that receive NSF support, refer to the PAPPG Chapter IX.B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAPPG Chapter IX.B contains the formal NSF requirements and expectations for institutional plans, allowable mechanisms, and oversight responsibilities related to RECR training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts of Interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF requires policies and training to identify and manage financial and other conflicts of interest that could affect research integrity, merit review, or stewardship of funds (see linked COI guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving human subjects compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Involving Human Subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators must comply with applicable human subjects protections (IRB review, informed consent, federal regulations) when NSF-funded research involves human participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving vertebrate animals compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Involving Vertebrate Animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF-funded projects involving vertebrate animals must follow institutional animal care and use policies and applicable regulations (IACUC oversight and related requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research security
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and institutions must manage risks to research security (e.g., safeguarding sensitive information, foreign influence concerns) in accordance with NSF guidance and institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review standards and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF's merit review process and standards (e.g., evaluation criteria, reviewer responsibilities) govern proposal evaluation; links include merit review guidance and expectations for reviewers and program officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panelist conflict of interest training
rubrics_metrics.description: Panelist Conflict of Interest Training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals serving on NSF review panels must receive COI training and follow procedures to disclose and manage conflicts when participating in merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper scholarship and attribution in proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper Scholarship and Attribution in Proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers must provide appropriate attribution, properly cite prior work, and avoid plagiarism or misrepresentation in proposals and related materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research results and sharing expectations (broader impacts, dissemination, public access, DMSP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research results and sharing: Broader Impacts; Dissemination and Sharing of Research Results; NSF Public Access Initiative; NSF Public Access Repository; Preparing Your Data Management and Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF expects investigators to plan for and execute dissemination and sharing of results, publications, and data (including preparing a Data Management and Sharing Plan), to address broader impacts, and to comply with NSF public access requirements and repository policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fostering harassment-free and inclusive working environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Treating colleagues with respect and fostering a harassment-free environment (Office of Civil Rights; Safe and Inclusive Working Environments for Off-Campus or Off-Site Research; Stopping Harassment and Assault).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and investigators must promote safe, inclusive, and harassment-free workplaces and field/research environments and follow OCR guidance and relevant institutional procedures for prevention and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct regulation and compliance (45 CFR 689)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Misconduct Regulation (45 CFR 689).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF-funded entities and investigators are subject to federal research misconduct regulations; allegations must be handled per 45 CFR 689 and institutional reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIG procedures for research misconduct investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Inspector General (OIG) Procedures for Research Misconduct Investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF's OIG has specified procedures for conducting investigations into allegations of research misconduct; institutions should be familiar with these investigative processes and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific integrity at NSF
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Integrity at NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF maintains policies and resources to ensure scientific integrity across funded research, including expectations for ethical conduct, transparency, and handling of allegations or concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research integrity in international contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting research in a global context, including when it involves international partners, can present opportunities and challenges that intersect with the responsible and ethical conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators engaged in international collaborations should be aware of cross-border legal, ethical, and policy issues affecting RECR and follow NSF guidance and institutional policies regarding international partnerships.
